short: Affluence at home, decolonisation abroad, and the Profumo affair at the end.
full:
Harold Macmillan took over in January 1957 with the Conservative Party shattered by Suez, and repaired relations with Washington within months. Presiding over rising wages and consumer spending, he told a Bedford crowd in 1957 that most of the country had never had it so good, and won the 1959 election comfortably.

In February 1960 he told the South African parliament that a wind of change was blowing through the continent, and his governments granted independence to Ghana, Nigeria, Tanganyika, Kenya and much of the rest of British Africa. He negotiated the Polaris missile deal with Kennedy in 1962 and applied to join the European Economic Community, only for de Gaulle to veto entry in January 1963. The Vassall spy case and then the Profumo affair wrecked his authority, and ill health prompted his resignation in October 1963.
